identity.name: Autonomous Action Audit-Trail Reconstruction Across Three Incident Classes — Identity Disable, Endpoint Isolate, Cloud Token Revoke
identity.summary: Fires three structurally different autonomous response actions in one run — identity disable, endpoint isolate, cloud token revoke — then measures whether EVERY executed action reconstructs to all five fields an auditor asks for: triggering input, reasoning trace, policy decision, approver identity, resulting change. The KPI is a completeness ratio, so it scores.
identity.description: 'Will the AI do something I cannot explain to my auditor' is the number-one blocker on autonomous response, and it is not answered by showing that a playbook fired. It is answered by taking an executed action and walking backwards from the change to the reasoning to the policy to the human who owned the decision. This card measures exactly that walk, and it measures it as a ratio so the answer is a number. Three trigger arms are used, and their structural difference is the point: an identity anomaly (a privileged principal signing in off its learned access baseline) resolving to an account disable, an endpoint anomaly (an off-baseline interpreter chain on a server-role host) resolving to a host isolation, and a cloud anomaly (an application access token used from an unseen calling location) resolving to a token revocation. One action class proves nothing about coverage: an audit trail can be complete for the one action the vendor demoed and threadbare for everything else, and a single-arm test cannot tell those apart. Each arm therefore contributes its own action row and each row is independently checked for all five reconstruction fields. Two things this deliberately does NOT prove, and both must be read aloud rather than buried. First, it proves the audit RECORD is complete and queryable; it does not prove the recorded reasoning is CORRECT. A model can log a coherent-looking rationale for a wrong action, and no query can adjudicate that. Second, it requires a real AgentiX / XSOAR tenant with governed-autonomy logging enabled. Without one the measurement resolves pending, never pass — which is the correct behaviour, because an absent audit trail and an unreachable tenant are different claims and reporting the second as the first would be the exact inflation the verdict taxonomy exists to prevent.

campaigns: Unit 42 2026 Global Incident Response Report — agentic operations compressing the attack lifecycle, and the governance question defenders must answer before granting an agent authority to act

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-APB-001 — governed-autonomy audit-trail reconstruction across three action classes.

prerequisites.description: A real AgentiX / XSOAR tenant with governed-autonomy action logging enabled. Without it every completeness measurement resolves pending, never pass — an absent audit trail and an unreachable tenant are different claims.

Three autonomous response policies are wired and permitted to act: identity disable, endpoint isolate, cloud token revoke. If only one is wired, the coverage claim collapses to that one action class and must be reported that way.

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE: no account is disabled, no host isolated and no token revoked
# against a real tenant. The three trigger arms emit labelled marker records so
# the tenant's own automation fires and writes its own action audit rows —
# which are the artifact under measurement.
set -euo pipefail
D=/tmp/cortexsim-apb001
RUN_TAG="${CORTEXSIM_RUN_TAG:-APB001}"
mkdir -p "$D"
# (1) identity arm -> expected autonomous action: disable-account
printf '{"run_tag":"%s","arm":"identity","event":"signin","principal":"svc-privileged@corp.local","source_ip":"203.0.113.55","privileged":true,"baseline_match":false}\n' "$RUN_TAG" > "$D/arm-identity.json"
# (2) endpoint arm -> expected autonomous action: isolate-endpoint
printf '{"run_tag":"%s","arm":"endpoint","event":"process","host_role":"server","parent":"httpd","child":"bash","cmdline":"bash -i","baseline_match":false}\n' "$RUN_TAG" > "$D/arm-endpoint.json"
# (3) cloud arm -> expected autonomous action: revoke-token
printf '{"run_tag":"%s","arm":"cloud","event":"api_call","oauth_token_id":"0CiSIMAPB001","caller_ip":"198.51.100.44","caller_seen_before":false}\n' "$RUN_TAG" > "$D/arm-cloud.json"
echo cortexsim-apb001-three-trigger-arms-emitted

input_variables.name: CORTEXSIM_RUN_TAG
input_variables.description: Run-scoped tag stamped onto every trigger record so a previous run's action rows cannot satisfy this run's completeness measurement.

expected_artifacts.description: An autonomous account-disable action row carrying its triggering input, reasoning trace, policy decision, approver identity and resulting change.
An autonomous endpoint-isolation action row with the same five reconstruction fields.
An autonomous token-revocation action row with the same five reconstruction fields.

abiocs.name: Identity Anomaly Trigger — Privileged Principal Sign-In Deviating From Its Learned Access Baseline
abiocs.description: Trigger arm one. A privileged principal authenticates from infrastructure absent from its learned calling baseline. This arm exists to CAUSE an autonomous account-disable, so the action row it produces can be walked backwards; the detection itself is well-trodden ground and is not the claim under test here.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001"
| filter is_privileged = true and baseline_match = false
| comp count() as signins, count_distinct(source_ip) as calling_ips by user_principal_name, result_type
| filter signins >= 1
| sort desc signins
| fields user_principal_name, result_type, calling_ips, signins
abiocs.causality_anchor: The privileged principal's own sign-in session owns this arm. It is deliberately disjoint from the endpoint and cloud arms so the three action rows are independent and single-arm audit completeness cannot masquerade as coverage.

abiocs.name: Endpoint Anomaly Trigger — Off-Baseline Interpreter Chain on a Server-Role Host
abiocs.description: Trigger arm two. A web-server parent spawns an interactive shell on a host whose learned role never does so. Structurally different from arm one — a process-causality anomaly rather than an identity anomaly — which is the whole reason three arms are run instead of one.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001"
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("httpd", "nginx", "apache2", "w3wp.exe")
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe")
| comp count() as spawns by agent_hostname, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name
| filter spawns >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name, spawns
abiocs.causality_anchor: The web-server process owns this arm's chain. Its causality_id is distinct from the identity and cloud arms, so the endpoint-isolation action row is independently attributable.

xql_queries.name: Cloud Anomaly Trigger — Application Access Token Used From an Unseen Calling Location
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7200)
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001"
| filter auth_type = "oauth_token" and caller_seen_before = false
| comp count() as api_calls, count_distinct(caller_ip) as calling_ips by oauth_token_id, connected_app
| filter api_calls >= 1
| sort desc api_calls
| fields oauth_token_id, connected_app, calling_ips, api_calls

xql_queries.name: Three Structurally Different Autonomous Actions Executed in One Run
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7200)
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001" and action_source = "cortex-agentix"
| comp count_distinct(action_type) as action_classes, count() as actions_taken by cortexsim_run_tag
| filter action_classes >= 3
| fields cortexsim_run_tag, action_classes, actions_taken

xql_queries.name: Autonomous Action Audit Completeness — All Five Reconstruction Fields Present
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7200)
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001" and action_source = "cortex-agentix"
| alter has_all_five = if(triggering_input_id != null and reasoning_trace_id != null and policy_decision != null and approver_identity != null and resulting_change_id != null, 1, 0)
| comp count() as actions_taken, sum(has_all_five) as actions_reconstructable by cortexsim_run_tag
| alter completeness_pct = multiply(divide(actions_reconstructable, actions_taken), 100)
| fields cortexsim_run_tag, actions_taken, actions_reconstructable, completeness_pct

xql_queries.name: Autonomous Action Reasoning Trace Resolves to Its Triggering Input
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7200)
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001" and action_source = "cortex-agentix"
| filter reasoning_trace_id != null and triggering_input_id != null
| comp count() as resolvable_actions, count_distinct(triggering_input_id) as distinct_triggers by action_type
| filter resolvable_actions >= 1
| sort desc resolvable_actions
| fields action_type, distinct_triggers, resolvable_actions

xql_queries.name: Approver Identity and Policy Decision Recorded for Every Autonomous Action
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7200)
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001" and action_source = "cortex-agentix"
| filter approver_identity != null and policy_decision in ("auto-approved", "human-approved", "policy-permitted")
| comp count() as governed_actions, count_distinct(approver_identity) as approvers by action_type, policy_decision
| sort desc governed_actions
| fields action_type, policy_decision, approvers, governed_actions

xql_queries.name: Resulting Change Is Independently Observable in the Target System
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7200)
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001" and action_source = "cortex-agentix"
| filter resulting_change_id != null and change_verified = true
| comp count() as verified_changes by action_type, resulting_change_kind
| sort desc verified_changes
| fields action_type, resulting_change_kind, verified_changes

xql_queries.name: Autonomous Actions Missing at Least One Reconstruction Field — the Audit Gap List
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7200)
| filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001" and action_source = "cortex-agentix"
| filter triggering_input_id = null or reasoning_trace_id = null or policy_decision = null or approver_identity = null or resulting_change_id = null
| comp count() as incomplete_actions by action_type
| sort desc incomplete_actions
| fields action_type, incomplete_actions

correlation_rules.name: Governed-Autonomy Audit Reconstruction Terminal Assertion
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(Identity Anomaly Trigger — Privileged Principal Sign-In Deviating From Its Learned Access Baseline) AND ABIOC(Endpoint Anomaly Trigger — Off-Baseline Interpreter Chain on a Server-Role Host) AND XQL(Cloud Anomaly Trigger — Application Access Token Used From an Unseen Calling Location) AND XQL(Three Structurally Different Autonomous Actions Executed in One Run) AND XQL(Autonomous Action Audit Completeness — All Five Reconstruction Fields Present) under one cortexsim_run_tag. The terminal assertion is a completeness RATIO, not a merge: every autonomous action executed in this run must reconstruct end to end to its triggering input, its reasoning trace, the policy decision that permitted it, the approver identity that owned it, and an independently observable resulting change. The bar is 100% of actions taken, across at least three structurally different action classes — one class proving complete says nothing about the other two, which is why a single-arm run cannot satisfy this rule. Failure is specific and reportable: the audit-gap list names each action missing a field, and the field it is missing. Two non-failures must be distinguished from failure. If no tenant is reachable or governed-autonomy logging is off, the measurement is PENDING, not a fail; and a complete audit record does NOT establish that the recorded reasoning was correct, only that it is present, attributable and queryable.

analytics_modules: Cortex AgentiX — governed-autonomy action logging with reasoning trace and approver attribution

products.evidence_query: dataset = xsiam_incidents | filter cortexsim_run_tag = "APB001" and action_source = "cortex-agentix" | comp count() as actions_taken, count_distinct(action_type) as action_classes by cortexsim_run_tag

threat_scenarios.name: Governed Autonomy — Audit-Trail Reconstruction Across Three Action Classes
threat_scenarios.description: Proves that every autonomous action taken in a run can be walked backwards from the change it made to the human who owned the decision, measured as a completeness ratio across three structurally different action classes rather than demonstrated on one.

threat_steps.objective: Three structurally different autonomous actions execute in one run — identity disable, endpoint isolate, cloud token revoke.
preconditions: All three autonomous response policies are wired and permitted to act.
Governed-autonomy action logging is enabled on the tenant.
steps: Fire the identity, endpoint and cloud trigger arms.
Confirm three distinct action_type values were executed under the run tag.
success_criteria: Both trigger ABIOCs fire and the cloud trigger query returns rows.

threat_steps.objective: Every executed action carries all five reconstruction fields, and the completeness ratio is 100%.
steps: Run the completeness query over every action row in the run.
Confirm the reasoning trace resolves to its triggering input for each action class.
Confirm approver identity and policy decision are recorded for each action class.
success_criteria: Reasoning-trace and approver queries each return one row per action class.

threat_steps.objective: The resulting change of each action is independently observable in the target system, not merely claimed by the action row.
steps: For each action class, confirm the change it claims to have made is visible in the target system.
Confirm change_verified is set for each.
success_criteria: One verified change row per action class.
No action claims a change that the target system cannot corroborate.

preventive_controls: Require an approver identity on every autonomous action policy, including the auto-approved path — 'the policy approved it' is only an answer if the policy itself has an owner.
Retain the reasoning trace for at least as long as the incident record it belongs to; a trace that expires before the audit is the same as no trace.
detection_engineering: Measure audit completeness as a ratio over ALL actions taken, not as a spot check on one. A vendor demo of one reconstructable action tells you nothing about the other action classes.
Check the resulting change against the target system rather than trusting the action row's own claim — an action that reports success while changing nothing is the failure mode that matters most.
Keep pending and fail separate. An unreachable tenant or disabled autonomy logging is not an audit failure, and reporting it as one manufactures false red.
